title: Test CCP2 half-duplex and finite receiver resources
description:
Scope: one CCP2 receiver-resource scenario module under /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/python/tests/sim/scenarios/, using the existing native-peer harness. Drive actual scheduling/radio events for owned grant without RX commitment, high-priority TX during committed RX, anonymous slot map, persistent hash collision, common-control return, finite passbands/demodulators and overlapping DODAGs. Compare to the independent interval/resource corpus. No new allocator, concurrency capability or idealized simultaneous one-radio reception may be introduced by the test.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Use finite declared resources and frozen expected traces. Keep this scenario family separate from capacity reporting and legal-accounting scenarios while sharing only transport/event adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Actual driver/tuning events never overlap forbidden RX/TX obligations or claim simultaneous reception on different channels with one radio. Sender grant alone cannot authorize an unavailable receiver, queue priority cannot preempt commitment, and anonymous ownership is rejected. Explicit assignment/repair explains collision resolution; channel count does not multiply RX/TX resources. Required control windows and declared passband/demodulator limits are observed in deterministic native-peer traces.
